findings.message: The Key field shows "✓ free · proposal ids …" whenever `check` is `{}` and no check is running. A live check that couldn't run is turned by `checkResultOf` into `check: {}` plus a notice. So a check that failed reads as a pass. The card shows "✓ free · proposal ids CON-001" next to "Couldn't check that just now." The same thing happens on first render: the state starts as `{}`, so the hint claims the key is free when nothing has been checked on this card, and a card can be days old. Fix: keep a separate verified flag, or a `checked` value per field. Set it only when a check actually comes back and passes for that field's current value. Show the ✓ hint only when it is set. A transient result clears it.
findings.scenario: Type key "CON" while the check request fails (DB blip or network) → checkFailure returns CHECK_FAILED → the card shows "✓ free · proposal ids CON-001" under Key, although CON is taken and was never checked.

findings.message: `pendingFor` swallows a failed `t.card()` and still makes the card. For a tool that has a `draft`, the model is only asked for the draft schema. So the input may be partial (`set_up_project` with `{}`, or `link_project_repo` with only `projectKey`). Without the card's `form`, the person has no fields to fill in. `confirmCard` then takes the `withAnswer` path, which returns the partial input unchecked, the service's schema rejects it, and the card is settled as failed for good. A card read that failed (`storedLink` or `clientsOf` hitting a DB error) ends up as a card that can never succeed, and the person is told "This couldn't be done". Fix: when `t.draft` is set and the card has no `form` (card failed or missing), don't propose. Either refuse with NOT_PROPOSED so the model says it couldn't prepare the card, or check the input against the full `t.input` first. Also check the input against `t.input` in the no-form confirm path.
findings.scenario: "link a repo to FLT" while the storedLink query throws → the card is shown with only the Project line and no Repo field → Link the repo → the service schema rejects the missing repoUrl → the card closes as "This couldn't be done … Nothing was changed."

findings.message: `<details open={filled || undefined}>` is controlled by whether the Repo URL has text. When the field is cleared, React removes the `open` attribute, the section collapses while the person is typing in it, and focus is left inside a hidden element. That breaks keyboard-complete use and Focus Order (WCAG 2.4.3). Fix: decide whether the section starts open once, from the initial values, and leave it uncontrolled after that. If a refusal names a field inside the section, open it with a ref; never close it from a value change.
findings.scenario: Open "Repo (optional)", type a URL, then select it all and press Backspace → `filled` becomes false → the details closes while the URL input still has focus, and a keyboard user loses their place.

findings.message: Key follows the name until Key is typed on the card. `typed` only counts keystrokes on the card, so a key the person gave in their message, or one the model filled from it, is overwritten with the name's initials as soon as the name is edited. A key can't change after creation (AC-4). Fix: start `follow` only when the key is empty or still equal to `initialsOf(start name)`. Treat a key that came in with the input as already typed.
findings.scenario: "set up a project called Northwind Portl (NWP)" → the card shows Key NWP → fix the name to "Northwind Portal" → Key silently becomes "NP" and the button reads "Create NP", so a project with the wrong, permanent key is created.

findings.message: If the person picks the Branch chip "other…" and leaves its text empty, `withEdits` deletes `defaultBranch` and the service quietly falls back to `main`. An empty required choice becomes a default the person explicitly moved away from. Fix: when the "other" chip is selected, the field is required. Send a marker from the client, or have the form treat an empty "other" as missing, and refuse with "Fill this in" on defaultBranch instead of defaulting.
findings.scenario: Repo URL https://github.com/example/x, choose Branch "other…", leave it blank, press "Create NWP and link repo" → the repo is linked on main and the receipt says "(main)", although the person chose another branch.

findings.message: `checkResultOf` turns a check that could not run (`CHECK_FAILED`, `transient`) into `check: {}`. That is the same value a passing check returns. `CardForm`'s `TextField` then treats `{}` as passed (`ok = check !== null && !check.message && !checking`) and shows the field's success hint. So a check that never ran tells the person the key is free, and the confirm button stays enabled. Fix: keep the failure state apart from a pass. For example, return `check: null` (or a separate `unknown` flag) for a transient failure, so `ok` is false and no ✓ hint is drawn. Still show the notice, and still don't block the button.
findings.scenario: The person types key CON, which Contoso Portal already uses. The live `checkCardField` call fails (DB timeout) and returns `CHECK_FAILED`. The card shows 'Couldn't check that just now.' and also '✓ free · proposal ids CON-001 · the key can't change later' under Key.

findings.message: The live check `onCheck` (a server action) has no timeout. While it is pending, `checking` stays true, and `blocked` includes `checking`, so the confirm button stays disabled until the request settles. Fix: race `onCheck` against a timeout that resolves to `CHECK_FAILED`.
findings.scenario: The server action stalls on a slow connection, so the 'Create NWP' button stays disabled with no message.

findings.message: `checkFailure` recognises a changed sign-in by the string `e.name === "SignedInElsewhere"`, while `apps/web/app/actions/chat.ts` imports the `SignedInElsewhere` class. If that class is renamed, the check silently falls through to the non-blocking transient failure. Fix: use `instanceof SignedInElsewhere`.
